title: Kid Rena comes looking for him
summary: Rena comes to his house looking for the banjo player who sat in and offers a Sunday night job.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yeah. So, uh, that night went on, but I didn't know what that night would mean. That would mean to me in the later years, you know. So, about a couple of months after that, uh, my wife's uncle, in all the past, said to me, he said, I heard Renner is looking for you, just like that. Kid Renner. Kid Renner. I said, well, Renner don't even, I said, Renner don't even know me. I don't know. He said, but that's what I heard. All right. So I didn't pay too much attention to that. But one day, I'm sitting on my step in the same black, right there on the first street. And I had my oldest boy, the boy that died. He was just about two years old. And I was sitting down on the step. It was a winter day, but the weather was warm and the sun was shining. I was sitting in the sun at the top. I saw Renner coming down the street, him and another fellow. And, uh, he come down the street and he stopped at my wife's uncle's house, the house I used to live in. The house knocked on the gate. I was on the side. Well, I knew Renner, but Renner didn't know me, you see. So I called over to him and I said to him, I said, I said, you're looking for a no? He said, no. He said, yes. He said, yes and then no too. He said, but I'm looking for a banjo player that lives around here named Richard. He said, yeah.

So I told him, I said, well, my name is Richard. He said, you play banjo? I said, yeah. He said, well, you must be the one I'm looking for. He crossed the street. So he said to me, he said, did you play over at Eli one night over there?
I said, well, I sit in and on a fella's place.
